title: Syllabub
subtitle: Whipped cream dessert with white wine and lemon
excerpt: Double cream whipped with white wine, lemon zest, and sugar until it holds a soft, pillowy peak. A light, elegant dessert that takes ten minutes to make and keeps in the fridge for several hours.

recipe.sourceNotes: Syllabub is one of the oldest English desserts. Early versions from the 16th and 17th centuries were made by milking a cow directly into a pail of wine or cider, producing a frothy drink. By the 18th century it had evolved into a whipped cream dessert, served in small glasses. There are two types: a firm whipped syllabub that holds its shape for hours, and an everlasting syllabub where the cream layer floats over a layer of sweetened wine. Both use the combination of cream, lemon, and wine that gives syllabub its distinctive taste. It is one of the few British desserts that genuinely requires no cooking at all. Serve in wine glasses or small tumblers with shortbread or sponge fingers alongside.

content.text: Macerate the lemon zest in the wine and lemon juice for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge, before adding the cream. This steeps the citrus oils into the wine and gives a much more vivid lemon flavour. Whip the cream to very soft peaks before adding the wine mixture, then continue to whip gently: the acid in the wine helps the cream hold its shape. Stop well before stiff peaks or the cream will become grainy.
Combine the white wine, lemon zest, lemon juice, and icing sugar in a bowl. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Pour the cold cream and vanilla into a large bowl. Whip to very soft peaks. Pour in the wine and lemon mixture in a steady stream, continuing to whip as you add it.
Continue to whip until the mixture holds a soft, billowy peak that just holds its shape. Do not over-whip. Spoon into glasses and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Serve with shortbread.
